belief: Anything I have could vanish tomorrow.
origins: A sudden loss of a job, a home, a loved one, or savings can teach us that nothing is safe. A parent who lost everything, or who lived in constant fear of loss, may have passed that fear along without a word. After a hard blow, the mind tries to protect us by expecting the next one.
teaches: Scripture is honest that earthly things can be lost. Jesus said moth, rust, and thieves can destroy what we store up on earth, and He pointed us to treasure that cannot be taken. God also gives a promise that does not depend on what we own: He will never leave us or forsake us. These verses do not say we will never lose anything. They say that what matters most is held securely, and that God is with us through every loss.
self_statements: Whatever I build can be taken away.
I cannot let myself get comfortable.
Just when things are good, something will happen.
I should not get attached to anything.
errors: Predicting loss before anything has happened.
Turning one painful loss into “everything is at risk.”
Treating a possible loss as certain and unbearable.
Dismissing what is stable and secure right now.
questions: What loss did I live through, and am I treating today as if it were that day?
What, right now, is secure and likely to stay?
If I did lose something, what has God given me to get through it?
What is the difference between being careful and living in dread?
What can I not lose, according to Scripture?
Who could stand with me in a hard time?
truth: Possessions and circumstances can change, and some losses are real. But I am not alone, and what matters most is held by God. I can be careful without living in dread, and enjoy what I have today without fearing every tomorrow.
hw_truths: God is with me, whatever happens to my things.
I can enjoy what I have today.
Being careful is wise; dread is not.
My most important treasure cannot be taken.
I have survived hard things before.
I do not face loss alone.
log: Each day, write down one thing that is secure and one fear about loss. Rate your fear from 0 to 10 and note any change.
actions: Make a short “what is secure” list.
Include people, faith, health, skills, and savings. Read it when fear about loss rises.
Update a document, review insurance, or back up important files. Then stop and rest.
Spend ten minutes enjoying something you have, such as a meal or a walk, and notice the fear without following it.
Tell one trusted person about a fear of loss.
Notice how it feels to share it.
prayer: Lord, You know the losses I have carried. Hold me when I fear more. Help me enjoy what You have given, and remind me that You will never leave me or forsake me. Amen.
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Anything I have could vanish tomorrow.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
hw_questions: What loss am I still reacting to?
What has God given me to cope with loss?
How can I be careful without dread?
